discoveries.choice: notes.txt holds exactly one line of free-form prose ("one line of notes") rather than structured, machine-parseable data such as JSON or key=value pairs.
discoveries.whyItMatters: The file is the phase's only deliverable; whether notes are prose or structured data determines whether downstream consumers can parse it programmatically at all, and therefore what the project's contract can guarantee.

alternatives.option: Machine-parseable structure (JSON object, YAML, or key=value lines)
alternatives.consequence: Adds schema and escaping concerns and requires a parser plus error handling, but makes the content reliably consumable by tooling instead of only by humans.
Zero parsing surface and maximum human flexibility, but any consumer must pattern-match text, so no field can be relied on programmatically.

recommendation.reason: Nothing in the phase demands programmatic access; keeping the note as plain text avoids inventing a schema that no consumer needs yet, and the format can be tightened later if a consumer appears.

discoveries.choice: The note carries no metadata or provenance (no author, timestamp, tags, or source reference) — the content is the note alone.
discoveries.whyItMatters: Provenance is what makes a note attributable and orderable over time; omitting it forecloses auditing, conflict resolution, and any later merge of notes from multiple sources, which is cheap to add now and awkward to backfill.

alternatives.option: Include a minimal header or metadata line (e.g. date/author/tag prefix)
alternatives.consequence: Every entry becomes attributable and sortable, at the cost of a small fixed format that must be parsed and maintained.

alternatives.option: Content only, no metadata, as written
alternatives.consequence: Simplest possible file, but the origin and recency of the note are unknowable, so later automated aggregation has no anchor.

recommendation.choice: Content only, no metadata, as written
recommendation.reason: For a single hand-written note, metadata would be speculative structure with no current reader; adding it later is a purely additive change (a new line), so deferring costs little.

discoveries.choice: The single note is terminated by a trailing newline and written as one physical line, with no bullet, numbering, or delimiter to separate future entries.
discoveries.whyItMatters: The line terminator and delimiter convention decide whether a future multi-note file is a well-formed POSIX text file and whether entries can be split/round-tripped without ambiguity.

alternatives.option: One entry per line with a blank-line or bullet separator convention established now
alternatives.consequence: Appending entries stays unambiguous and diff-friendly, but commits the project to a separator rule before a second entry exists.

alternatives.option: Single newline-terminated line with no separator convention, as written
alternatives.consequence: The file is a valid, diff-friendly text file and appending is trivial, but a later multi-entry format must define its own separator and may need migration.

recommendation.choice: Single newline-terminated line with no separator convention, as written
recommendation.reason: Line-per-entry is the natural default that a future multi-note file will almost certainly adopt anyway, so no explicit convention is needed yet and nothing is lost by waiting.

discoveries.choice: The note text is lowercase and unpunctuated ("one line of notes") — no capitalization, no terminating period, no emphasis markers.
discoveries.whyItMatters: Stylistic conventions set readability and consistency expectations for all future notes; fixing them now makes the file uniform, while leaving them unset means every later entry chooses independently.

alternatives.consequence: Reads as conventional prose and matches most documentation style guides, but is a rule that must be applied consistently by every future writer.
Fast to write and clearly informal, but produces inconsistent-looking content as the file grows.

recommendation.reason: With one informal scratch note, enforcing a prose style guide adds process without benefit; consistency can be imposed retroactively if the file becomes a shared artifact.
